messages:
Ashley Nguyen: FYI customer acme-corp hit quota mid-cycle after a large ingestion burst and never saw credits refill at their local midnight. They started getting 429s and said console still shows 0 even after local reset :thinking:

Omar Patel: which org id + plan? do we have their timezone set on the org?

Ashley Nguyen: org_987, pay-as-you-go, no rollover. Billing tz set to America/Los_Angeles according to our onboarding record. They reported heavy usage ~2026-04-30 21:10 PDT and exhaustion ~21:45 PDT. Expected refill 2026-05-01 00:00 PDT but still 0 at 00:05 and 01:00. Attached logs and sample curl below.

Priya Singh: pinging billing infra. first pass: our resets are computed in UTC but we convert to org tz for display. possible mismatch between computed next_reset and console UI rendering. can you paste the exact API response?

Ashley Nguyen: here's the failed request + response (redacted keys):

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":1000}'
```

Response:
```json
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{
  "error": "quota_exhausted",
  "message": "Monthly credits exhausted. Next reset at 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

Omar Patel: interesting — response says next reset at 00:00:00Z (UTC). For America/Los_Angeles that is 2026-04-30 17:00 PDT (previous day 5pm). that would be the opposite of what customer expects. can you confirm the response time and the request timestamps?

Ashley Nguyen: request timestamp (server-received) 2026-04-30T21:45:12-07:00. The response body above literally says 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z which would be 17:00 PDT on 4/30 — which makes no sense given the customer expected midnight local. I'm guessing the billing computation used the org's period_end (2026-05-01T00:00:00 in org-local) but then we accidentally appended Z without converting.

Priya Singh: pulling DB now. Query I ran:
```sql
SELECT org_id, billing_tz, period_end_local, period_end_utc FROM org_billing WHERE org_id='org_987';
-- returns: org_id='org_987', billing_tz='America/Los_Angeles', period_end_local='2026-05-01 00:00:00', period_end_utc='2026-05-01 07:00:00+00'
```

Priya Singh: So the canonical period_end_utc is 2026-05-01 07:00:00Z (00:00 PDT + 7h). The API response showing 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z looks like we formatted the local time as if it were Zulu. that's a serialization bug: we send the local timestamp string but tag it with Z.

Sasha (oncall): that would make the customer think next reset is earlier/later incorrectly. customers in PDT expecting midnight would see a mismatch. we need to check both the token issuance check (quota evaluator) and the UI read path. if evaluator compares now() < next_reset_utc but next_reset_utc is wrong, it will block incorrectly.

quota-bot: @eng-infra flagged issue #INC-4212: suspected timezone serialization bug in billing service. Priority: P1 (customer-facing outage risk).

Omar Patel: short repro for devs: create org with billing_tz=America/Los_Angeles, set period_end_local to 2026-05-01 00:00:00, then call quota status endpoint and observe JSON output. sample SQL & curl below.

```sql
INSERT INTO org_billing (org_id, billing_tz, period_end_local) VALUES ('org_test_tz','America/Los_Angeles','2026-05-01 00:00:00');
-- run job that backfills period_end_utc from local tz
SELECT period_end_local, period_end_utc FROM org_billing WHERE org_id='org_test_tz';
```

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/org_test_tz/quota_status
# look at "next_reset" field in JSON, verify timezone annotation
```

Ashley Nguyen: customer impact: they were blocked from serving production traffic for ~3 hours until we manually top-up their org by 100k credits. They want an explanation and timeline.

Priya Singh: immediate mitigation steps we took: 1) manual top-up to restore service (ticket billing-8791), 2) backfilled period_end_utc for org_987 to canonical UTC value, 3) opened INC-4212 and assigned to eng-infra (Amir).

Sasha (oncall): long-term fixes we need: - fix serialization so next_reset in API responses is in ISO-8601 with correct offset (e.g., 2026-05-01T07:00:00Z) or include explicit tz field - add end-to-end integration test for DST/zone conversions - surface both UTC and local next_reset in console with a hover explanation - consider sending a push/email warning when a burst exhausts credits inside a billing day (esp for orgs in non-UTC tz)

Omar Patel: customer comms draft: "we found a bug in how we display reset times for non-UTC orgs which caused the API/UI to show an incorrect reset timestamp. We have restored service via a one-time top-up and deployed a fix to ensure reset times are shown in both UTC and your local timezone. We're following up with timeline and root cause in the incident report." :thumbsup:

Ashley Nguyen: customer accepted the top-up and asked for ETA on permanent fix. I'll reply with the mitigation steps + link to INC-4212 and promise ETA after eng reassigns. Also asked if we can temporarily enable burst capacity for them, Sasha?

Sasha (oncall): I can enable temporary burst exemption for org_987 for next 48h, will record change in changelog and notify ops.

Priya Singh: follow-ups for billing team: create a backfill job to scan orgs created before timezone fix and flag any where period_end_local was serialized as UTC; add a weekly audit that checks period_end_local -> period_end_utc consistency. I'll own this.

Omar Patel: notes for KB: add FAQ entry "Why did my monthly credits not refill at midnight?" explaining UTC vs local tz, how we display times, and what to do if blocked (contact support for temp top-up).

Ashley Nguyen: thanks folks — I'll send the customer update now and mark thread for follow-up after INC-4212 lands. :eyes:

Sasha (oncall): leaving a final note: if you see other customers with similar symptom (midnight vs console mismatch), please ping me and include org_id + sample API response.
